Reporter asks how to unit test code that calls future.join() on a CompletableFuture returned by supplyAsync(...).thenApplyAsync(...), with oracleRepo.extractSpecificNameAndEventTypes and sendNameData mocked. final: {"number": 1691, "label": "question", "route": "answer", "related": [2819, 806, 1117], "evidence": ["mockito/mockito-core/src/main/java/org/mockito/Mockito.java"], "reply": "Mockito has no special support for CompletableFuture, and you don't need any. The async chain is plain Java, so test it like any other code. Stub the repository with Mockito.when(oracleRepo.extractSpecificNameAndEventTypes(firstName, lastName)).thenReturn(map), and do the same for extractAllNameAndEventTypes. Create oracleRepo with Mockito.mock(...). Pass async as false so future.join() blocks, then assert on the returned list. Use Mockito.verify(...) to check the repository calls. Examples are in the Javadoc of mockito-core/src/main/java/org/mockito/Mockito.java."}
